title: Improve thread-safety
body:
1. Eliminate `yices_smt2_mt` frontend, incorporating multi-thread test functionality into `yices_smt2`.
2. Provide a thread-safe implementation of timeouts.
3. Avoid allocating very large arrays on the stack. (Noticed because it caused threads, which have smaller stacks, to crash.) Variable-sized allocation on the stack is a bad idea if the allocation size is not bounded.
4. For testing purposes, give thread stacks the same size as the main stack. (Necessary to work around the fact that libcudd uses recursion where it should use iteration in at least one place.)
5. Enhance check.sh to allow passing additional options to tests and to allow running individual tests.
6. Clean up error-handling for POSIX threads API.
7. Fix incorrect order of destruction in `yices_exit`.

With these changes, all regression tests pass with `--enable-mcsat --enable-thread-safety` when running the `yices_smt2` frontend with 8 threads.

title: "FATAL ERROR: unexpected context status" when using (get-model) on an 'unknown' result
body:
Hi there!

I'm currently trying out the timeout option (-t) for a SMT2 project.
I'm sending in a bunch of assertions, with a call to (check-sat), and then to (get-model).

As expected, I get the right model when the result is 'sat', and an error when the result is 'unsat' since (get-model) is not supposed to be called in that case.
However when a (check-sat) command times out, the result given by (check-sat) is 'unknown', and it seems yices2 does not known how to handle (get-model) in that case.

Here's what I'm getting :

```
unknown

*************************************************************
FATAL ERROR: BUG: unexpected context status
*************************************************************
Please report this bug to yices-bugs@csl.sri.com.
To help us diagnose this problem, please include the
following information in your bug report:

  Yices version: 2.6.2
  Build date: 2022-06-27
  Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (release)

Thank you for your help.
*************************************************************

BUG: unexpected context status
```

This is a problem, since according to the [SMT-LIB documentation](https://smtlib.cs.uiowa.edu/papers/smt-lib-reference-v2.6-r2021-05-12.pdf) :

> On reporting sat or unknown the solver should move to sat mode—and then respond to
get-assignment, get-model, and get-value commands provided that the corresponding
enabling option is set to true.

Here's a random sudoku.txt file which should easily time out and recreate the bug. Just launch :
```
yices-smt2 -t 3 sudoku.txt
```

[sudoku.txt](https://github.com/SRI-CSL/yices2/files/9055307/sudoku.txt)

title: SMT2 frontend does not flush output after responding to some commands
body:
Under certain conditions the SMT2 frontend does not flush the output after reporting the command results. This greatly frustrates interacting with yices from another program. These errors can be observed by running `yices-smt2 | cat`. Piping the output through cat is essential as it disables the default line-buffering of the terminal.

So far I have observed this with the following commands:

- check-sat-assuming with default options in non-incremental mode
- check-sat with produce-unsat-cores in non-incremental mode

title: Requesting improved smt2 array support
body:
I understand that yices doesn't differentiate between arrays, and functions internally, but I was wondering if the output while using the `--smt2-model-format` flag could have an option to output the result as an array if the input was an array (or as a function if the input was a function)? Currently, the output being a function when the input was an array makes it harder to use the result in some of the other solvers (e.g. z3, and cvc5) as they seem to differentiate between the two.

Current output:
```
(define-fun params ((x!0 Int)) Int (ite (= x!0 6) 5 (ite (= x!0 5) 2 (ite (= x!0 4) 2 (ite (= x!0 3) 0 (ite (= x!0 2) 1 14))))))
```

Desired output (I hand translated this, so I may have made minor mistakes, but I think it is correct):
```
(define-fun params () (Array Int Int) (store (store (store (store (store ((as const (Array Int Int)) 14) 2 1) 3 0) 4 2) 5 2) 6 5))
```

Ideally, yices would also support `(as const (Array Int Int))` inputs too, but I assume that would be more work. Unfortunately, this means that a separate flag probably is needed (to enable outputting arrays as arrays) as otherwise yices could produce smtlib2 formats that it couldn't read.

Edit: The `((as const (Array Int Int)) 14)` syntax appears to be non-standard smt-lib syntax that cvc4, z3, mathsat, and possibly more provers support. I would still appreciate this being supported, but it doesn't appear to be specified in the standards anywhere that I can find, and I see some comments elsewhere on the internet saying it isn't part of the standard. :/

title: Idea to improve speed with my Yices usage?
body:
Hi all,

First of all thank you for this solver! I use it everyday inside a binary tool analysis that I am developing for my thesis. I don't know if you can help me but I will try anyway.

## Context

My project is a C++ program whose goal is to build the control flow graph of an unknown binary program. The idea is to alternate between static disassembly and symbolic execution until a fixed point. At the fixed point we hope to have all the assembly instructions code of the program.

## What about Yices?

In order to symbolically execute some pieces of the program I use SMT solvers (already tried Z3, CVC4, boolector and Yices but Yices seems to be the faster solver for my usage).

Let's say I want to symbolically execute some assembly instructions with specific entries values. My process is to "translate" assembly code in SMTLIBv2 formula:

`x86 instructions --> intermediate language --> SMTLIBv2 formula`

My final step is to give the SMTLIBv2 formula to Yices in order to obtain the SAT values of the registers and memory cells at the end of the symbolic execution. To do that I simply use `assert` for my entry contrains, `define-fun` for my variables updates and `check-sat` and `get-values` to obtain final values. Also, I use BitVector variables for my CPU registers and a BitVector array to represent the memory).

## Simple example

Let's say I have this piece of code that I want to symbolically execute:

```asm
ADD EBX, EAX    ; EBX <-- EAX + EBX
SUB ECX, EBX    ; ECX <-- ECX - EBX
```

Also, I have the current entry values: `EAX = 0x1`, `EBX = 0x2` and `ECX = 0x8`.
Of course, "by hand" we can easily find that at the end of this execution we will have `EAX = 0x1`, `EBX = 0x3` and `ECX = 0x5`, but we will use Yices to do that:

After the translation I obtain this final SMTLIB formula:

```SMT
(set-option :produce-models true)
(set-logic QF_ABV)

; Variables declaration
(declare-fun eax0 () (_ BitVec 32))
(declare-fun ebx0 () (_ BitVec 32))
(declare-fun ecx0 () (_ BitVec 32))

; Entry contraints
(assert (= eax0 (_ bv1 32)))
(assert (= ebx0 (_ bv2 32)))
(assert (= ecx0 (_ bv8 32)))

; Code instructions representation
(define-fun ebx1 () (_ BitVec 32) (bvadd ebx0 eax0))    ; ADD EBX, EAX
(define-fun ecx1 () (_ BitVec 32) (bvsub ecx0 ebx1))    ; SUB ECX, EBX

; Get final values
(check-sat)
; Do not ask for EAX final value because I already know that EAX register is not modified by this code
(get-value (ebx1 ecx1))
```

## How is it in the real world?

Of course this exemple is really simple but in reality I need to deal with bigger formula (no more that ~30 assembly instructions).
I noticed that during the execution of my tool, 90% of the time is spend in Yices (during the `(check-sat)` step I guess?).
For a "simple" binary program I have to apply ~1000000 SMTLIB formula to Yices (so ~1000000 `(check-sat)`, `get-value` and `(reset)`).
This is what I currently do in order to obtain the best time:

* I do not give unused contrains in the formula (in my previous exemple, I will not put `(assert (= edx0 (_ bv24 32)))` because I already know that the `EDX` register is not used by my instructions)
* I call `(reset)` between each symbolic execution (also, I do not use `(push)` and `(pop)` commands)
* I communicate with Yices through pipes with a subprocess (I use [reproc library](https://github.com/DaanDeMeyer/reproc) and I open Yices with `yices-smt2 --bvconst-in-decimal` command)

## Idea to improve my usage of Yices

I know that this is not really an issue because Yices works well for my usage. But I am wondering if I can improve my process somewhere in order to reduce the time I spend using Yices in my program. Of course if I can win some milliseconds on every call to Yices at the end it worth it 😉.

* Should I use the C API instead of my `fork-execv-pipe`? (IIRC, last time I checked the C API does not offer `get-value` with multiple variables. Also, my intermediate language directly give me each assembly instruction in SMTLIBv2 format so I need to parse each SMTLIB command to use C objects of the API)
* Can I "by-pass" the `(check-sat)` step because I already know that the formula is `SAT`? But I guess that this step is mandatory to obtain the model and use `get-value`?
* Do I miss something else?

Thank you very munch for the time spend reading this message and for your help!

title: Mcsat bv
body:
Added the normalisation of bv_polys so that coefficients are always odd (otherwise we use shifts to transfer a power of 2 from the monomial coefficient to the monomial variable).
This seems to help. The arith bv explainer can thus treat multiplications by powers of two...

Added a function to check correctness of rewrites by using regular yices. It is triggered by ```--trace mcsat::bv::rewrite::check```. Added this option to most of the regress tests.

title: Output "Decimal" Bitvectors
body:
Yices2 seems to accept bitvector constants with decimal numerals as described in the SMTLib extension for bitvectors (under extensions in http://smtlib.cs.uiowa.edu/logics-all.shtml#QF_BV).
- Bitvector Constants:
    (_ bvX n) where X and n are numerals, i.e. (_ bv13 32),
    abbreviates the term #bY of sort (_ BitVec n) such that
    [[#bY]] = nat2bv[n](X) for X=0, ..., 2^n - 1.

However, it seems to output bitvectors as binary literals ("#b" followed by bits) by default. Could you add an option to output these "decimal" bitvectors?
